correctness_confidence.basis: The machine-verified theorems (Lean endpoints) are rigorously checked and highly trustworthy, but the prose abstract overclaims their composition into the final area law.

novelty.basis: Formalizing continuous gauge theory reductions, Haar measures, and Migdal moves in Lean 4 is a significant and novel contribution to computational mathematical physics.

reproducibility.basis: The paper lists precise commit hashes, Lean definitions, and standard Mathlib dependencies, enabling clear static inspection of the formal artifact boundaries.

rigor.basis: Lean 4 provides exceptional rigor for the formalized parts, though the textual abstract lacks rigor in matching the precise boundaries of the verified code.

significance.basis: Provides a robust foundational library and methodology for eventually achieving a fully verified 2D YM exact solution, even if this version falls short of the full claim.

potential_errors: The text claims 'the claimed contribution is their concrete end-to-end machine-checked composition'. This phrasing incorrectly implies the end-to-end composition to the original-edge area law is fully verified, contradicting the limitations explicitly stated in Section 10.
strengths: Provides a highly rigorous, machine-verified Lean 4 formalization of the 2D YM heat-kernel measure and Migdal subdivision moves.
Successfully formalizes integration of the S^3 Haar measure, character convolutions, and exact heat-kernel semigroups.
The manuscript is ultimately transparent about its limitations in Section 10, cleanly demarcating what is kernel-checked from what remains open.
strong_novelty_candidates: Machine-checked formalization of character convolution and infinite heat-kernel semigroup limits for SU(2) YM in Lean 4.
Formalized explicit two-face Migdal subdivision move via genuine Haar integration.
summary: The manuscript presents a Lean 4 formalization of several key components of the exact heat-kernel solution for two-dimensional SU(2) Yang-Mills theory. It successfully machine-checks the Haar measure on SU(2), orbital integration, character convolution, and Migdal subdivision moves. However, as acknowledged in the attached supersession notice and Section 10, this specific version contains a material gap: it does not complete the global spanning-tree gauge fixing required to link the post-gauge-fixed evaluator to the original-edge physical integral for arbitrary cellulations. Consequently, the title and abstract overclaim the extent of the end-to-end 'Exact Simple-Loop Area Law' verified herein. While the verified mathematical components are rigorous and represent a novel formalization effort in mathematical physics, the discrepancy between the stated main result in the abstract and the actual verified scope necessitates a major revision to align the text claims with the formally proven endpoints.
unresolved_material_objections: The abstract and title claim the 'Exact Simple-Loop Area Law' and an end-to-end exact identity for E[Wn(C)], but Section 10 concedes the formalization does not yet lift the transformation to all original edge variables for arbitrary cellulations, leaving the main physical integral claim incomplete in this version.
weaknesses: The title and abstract severely overstate the scope of the machine-verified theorems in this specific version, masking the mathematical gap between the post-gauge-fixed evaluator and the original-edge integral.
